newsitem.title: USA: Calif. counties to sue R.J. Reynolds over ads.
newsitem.headline: Calif. counties to sue R.J. Reynolds over ads.

text.p: Eleven California counties and City of San Jose said Thursday they would join a lawsuit against R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co, challenging "Joe Camel" advertising that allegedly targets children.
The lawsuit seeks an injunction, in addition to civil penalties and the refund of profits from R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co, a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp.

If the lawsuit is successful, attorneys for the California governments said R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co could be forced to turn over hundreds of millions of dollars in profits from the controversial advertising campaign.
"I can't put Joe Camel's creators in jail," said San Francisco's attorney, Louise Renne. "But I can lighten their wallets."

Renne told reporters that the 11 California counties, including San Francisco and the city of San Jose filed a joint motion on Thursday in state Superior Court to join the 1991 Mangini lawsuit against R.J. Reynolds Tobacco.
The case is set for trial in December. It would be the first major tobacco lawsuit to go to trial in the state.
A spokesperson for R.J. Reynolds Tobacco was not immediately available to comment on the lawsuit.
"The evidence will show that they knowingly sought to target young people," Renne said. "We are out to stop that."

The lawsuit alleges that R.J. Reynolds Tobacco's "Joe Camel" campaign "aids and abets" the violation of state law because it is illegal to sell cigarettes to minors, San Francisco attorney Elizabeth Laporte said.
The "Joe Camel" lawsuit will be the third filed by the California local governments. They have already filed suits against tobacco companies in federal and state court.
"We are now on a three course path," Renne said. "We are not going away."

The counties have been in contact with officials representing Liggett Group. Liggett Group has "indicated a willingness to help us" in the "Joe Camel" lawsuit, plaintiffs' attorney Patrick Coughlin said.

Earlier this month, Liggett Group, owned by Bennett LeBow's Brooke Group Ltd, broke ranks with other tobacco companies by agreeing to settle with 22 state attorneys general who sued the industry to recoup smoking- related Medicaid health care costs.
The state of California, the most populous state, with potentially billions of dollars in claims, has so far not sued the tobacco industry.
